evidence:
Evidence scope for the implementation PR split: the observations below are
inherited from the larger, uncommitted qualification tree. That tree also
contained the separate MEM-1G components, larger private-memory contract ceilings,
and twenty-restart fixture; those changes are not part of this backlog-only
split. Its image hashes, root digest, workload results, mutation counts and test
results do not identify or qualify the split's binaries. The split retains the
previous admitted capacity and lifecycle limits. Fresh split validation passed root tests (261/261), host tests, formatter,
full lint, Ruff, docs/tasks and marker controls (1848 rejected mutations).
`just private_memory_check` passed the unchanged 64 MiB ARM/RV64 paths and
ARM failure-injection cases, including the extracted ownership ledger.
`just lifecycle_restart_check` passed its unchanged three-restart policy.
The split root tree identity is
`ef6fb9b46dad2dbe282691baaaf0fe93a8ebf0771bffdeb2e0af9cda54f1719a`;
exact split image hashes are recorded in the closure evidence of prerequisite
`01a0ae12-4ddf-79b4-a086-266941fd8ba5`. Generated closures and dependent run
identities accompany this split. These results do not claim split-binary 1 GiB
or physical-board qualification.

Observed on 2026-09-17 in the implementation tree based on
`90a184fb383ed9bfd800a243a32dd4e4ee06007b`; the tested `slime-root` tree digest is
`4a07cd403cf5a53fa5d15741c827b33f9623194fd7a34d8107290a063c9d7a9c`.
The exact packaged images are ARM
`15020aa62735448268a94ddd9ed873b72db5c5faa26900e6374047c909716bac`
and RV64
`48ffa9115192bc652df1f3215e05233a435f22dc522a29bd39b783e6d8a7ea65`.
Both use pinned QEMU 11.0.1, one CPU, and respectively 2048/3072 MiB.
This evidence names tested dirty-tree binaries, not the unchanged base commit.

Both capacity executions completed four resident 256 MiB holders, twenty fault
and replacement cycles, and final teardown. While private memory was full,
holder A repeatedly created a one-page shared buffer, refused a second create,
refused private-window collision, mapped at a different leaf-table range on each
round, checked every served word zero, wrote/read data, sealed, unmapped and
released. Its one-page/one-buffer/one-mapping declaration was not widened.
Forty such rounds reused backing without a change in equivalent-phase free slots,
ordinary/reusable capacity, private page charge or descriptor counts.

The global-prefix prerequisite's exclusive range ledger independently accounts
for the complete cold-baseline-to-teardown transition with zero residual on both
targets. Its record `01a0ae12-4ddf-79b4-a086-266941fd8ba5` contains the complete
ledger totals, transcript identities and verification boundaries. Retained
backing and parent CSlots remain explicitly owned; they are not mislabeled free.

`just test_sel4_root` passed 261/261 tests across 21 modules, including failed
buddy split/revoke, anchor delete/revoke retry, partial teardown quarantine,
mapping-table cleanup retry, VSpace lifetime separation, pending retirement
ordering/capacity, reserved cleanup timer capacity, receiver-only loans and
foreign-VSpace orphan settlement before frame reuse. These host injections cover
the actual owning transition paths; no physical kernel-failure campaign is
claimed. Runtime loan/sample gates retained owner-release and peer-death semantics.
The root now retains a retiring VSpace until IO, committed buffers, receiver-only
loans, orphan mappings and pending alias cleanup are settled, with timer-paced
retry rather than waiting for unrelated IPC.

The final behavioral regression sequence passed `just test_host`,
`just sel4_root_boot_check`, `just sel4_reclamation_check`,
`just sel4_loan_check`, `just sel4_sample_check`, `just io_block_check`,
`just lifecycle_restart_check`, `just private_memory_check`, and
`just private_memory_cycles_check`, plus Rust fmt/lint and Ruff. After adding
ownership diagnostics, both capacity runs and root tests/fmt/lint/Ruff passed
again. The marker control gate passed 1848 mutations, eight identity cases and
four runtime cases; docs/tasks checks passed before closure. Independent read-only
reviews identified and then confirmed fixes for alias cleanup, seal rollback,
VSpace retirement, IO page-progress and cross-VSpace orphan references; the final
exit audit found both prerequisite bug exits covered.

This closes the exposed shared-buffer capacity leak, not MEM-1G's remaining
isolation/qualification coverage, arbitrary adaptive capacity, or any physical
board claim. Raw transcripts remain local diagnostic artifacts under `build/`,
with exact hashes recorded in the global-prefix prerequisite; remote archival
retention is not asserted.
